sections.name: 1.1 A Day at the Beach (counting objects in a picture)

concepts.text: Count objects in a busy picture (coconuts, boats, children, oranges) and write the totals
Reflect on counting one by one versus counting in bunches or groups
Grouping makes counting large collections faster and easier

sections.name: 1.2 Let us Do: Shops on the beach (counting in groups)

concepts.text: Count items arranged in equal groups (necklaces of 10 shells each)
Count equal groups plus loose items (6 groups of 4 balloons and 2 extra)
Count bunches plus loose items (bunches of bananas and loose bananas)
Find the number of groups and the number in each group (bracelets of 5 shells, necklaces of 10)
Same total can be made from different groupings (10 groups of 5 vs 5 groups of 10)

sections.name: 1.3 Let us Think: Things that come in tens

concepts.text: Name everyday things sold or packed in tens (pencils, biscuits, toffees)

sections.name: 1.4 Tasty Chikoos! (trays of ten and loose ones)

concepts.text: One tray holds 10 chikoos; count trays to find the total (8 trays = 80)
Split a number into full trays of ten and loose ones (25 = 2 trays and 5 loose)
Represent 2-digit numbers like 43, 35, 58 as tens and ones
Let us Match: match a number to its picture of trays and loose items

sections.name: 1.5 Fun with Blocks and Strips (place value)

concepts.text: A block stick is made of 10 single blocks
A ten strip stands for 10 units; a single square is one unit
Count sticks and units shown and write the number
Complete a table writing numbers as tens and units
Tens and ones: the left digit tells tens, the right digit tells ones
10 tens make 100 (one hundred)
Count on in ones and in tens to complete a count up to 100
Combine strips of two colours to make a total of 100
Draw tens and ones cards to show a given number
Fill in blanks writing a number from its tens and ones (e.g. 4 tens 7 ones = 47)
Expand a 2-digit number into tens and ones
Compare two numbers by looking at tens first (27 is less than 72 because 2 tens < 7 tens)
Reversed digits make different numbers (67 and 76, 53 and 35)
Fill in 'more' or 'less' to compare two quantities
Write a number that is more than or less than a given number
When tens are equal, compare the ones

sections.name: 1.9 Let us Play: Flash Card Game (making numbers from digit cards)

concepts.text: Use digit cards 0-9 in tens and ones places to make 2-digit numbers
Make a number greater than 50 / less than 30 / between two numbers
Smallest 2-digit number is 10; largest 2-digit number is 99
Explain why 99 is the largest 2-digit number (100 has three digits)
Swap two digit cards and compare the two numbers formed
Make the largest and smallest number from two given digits
Arrange numbers in decreasing order (largest to smallest) along a path
Ordering numbers in increasing order (smallest to largest)

sections.name: 1.11 Play with Numbers: Who am I?

concepts.text: Riddles about 2-digit numbers: largest, smallest, with or without repeated digits
Largest 2-digit number with different digits (98); smallest with repeated digits (11)
Find numbers with a given digit in the tens or ones place (smallest with 3 tens = 30)
Make up your own 'Who am I?' number riddles
Ordinal positions in a boat race: first, second, third, fourth, fifth
Identify which boat is in a given position and the position of a given boat
Read a month calendar to find the day on which a festival falls (Onam)
Find the date of a festival or national day (Independence Day, 15 August)
Find the date when given the day of the week (Raksha Bandhan)

sections.name: 2.1 Let us Do: Musical instruments and their shapes

concepts.text: Observe musical instruments (drum, matka/ghatam, shehnai, harmonium) and their shapes
Find instruments shaped like a drum (cylinder)
Find instruments shaped like a matka (round, sphere-like)
Compare shapes of two instruments (harmonium is box-like/cuboid, drum is cylinder)
Share experiences of seeing or playing musical instruments
Name solid shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere
Match everyday objects and instruments to their solid shapes
Cross the odd one out in a group of objects by shape
Real-life examples: dice (cube), box/brick (cuboid), can (cylinder), ice-cream cone (cone), ball (sphere)
Difference between flat (2D) and solid (3D) shapes

sections.name: 2.3 Let us Do: Decorating shapes (faces, edges, corners)

concepts.text: A face is a flat surface of a solid; some solids have curved surfaces
An edge is where two faces meet; a corner is where edges meet
Count stars needed to decorate every face (cube needs 6)
Count ribbon stripes needed for every edge (cube needs 12)
Count pompom balls needed for every corner (cube has 8)
Cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners
Cone has 1 corner and 1 flat face; sphere has no corners or edges
Cylinder has 2 flat faces and a curved surface, no corners

sections.name: 2.4 Let us Think: Sorting objects in a table

concepts.text: Observe objects and fill a table by their shape or properties
Objects with curved surfaces can roll; objects with flat faces can slide or be stacked
Name objects that have a given number of faces or corners
Name objects having no corners, one corner, or many corners
Make a solid with four faces from a cardboard sheet
Think of and make an object with only one face (curved surface)

sections.name: 3.1 Look at the Ginladi (bead counter to 100)

concepts.text: Count the 100 beads on a ginladi arranged in tens
Write missing numbers on blank cards by counting beads
Make number cards (38, 44, 58, 65, 98) and place them on the ginladi

sections.name: 3.2 Number strip: moving forward and backward

concepts.text: Count steps forward on a number strip to reach a target
Move back and forward by given steps and find the ending number
Moving forward adds; moving backward takes away

sections.name: 3.3 Let us Play: Guess my Place (number line)

concepts.text: Read the number at a marked point on a number line
Mark a given number (65, 79) on a number line
Skip count forward in 3s (1, 4, 7, 10...)
Skip count forward in 5s (40, 45, 50...)
Skip count forward in 10s (50, 60, 70...)
Find the rule of a number pattern and extend it

sections.name: 3.5 Let us Do: Skip counting on the number chart

concepts.text: Mark numbers reached by skip counting in 2s and in 5s on a 1-100 chart
Numbers common to counting in 2s and 5s are the tens (10, 20, ... 100)
Numbers common to 2s, 3s and 5s within 100 (30, 60, 90)
Numbers common to counting in 5s and 7s (35, 70)
Make a number line on the ground and jump along it
Decide whether counting in steps from a start lands on a target (10 in 10s reaches 100)
Counting in 2s from an even start never lands on an odd number (4 never reaches 17)
Check if a target can be reached when counting in 3s or 5s
Number just before a given number
Count backward from 10 to 1
Skip count backward in 3s, 5s, 10s and 20s
Check if a sequence has a pattern; change numbers to make one and extend it

sections.name: 3.8 Let us Talk: Reasoning with counting

concepts.text: Counting on from a number never includes numbers before it
Decide if a number appears when counting in 2s from a start
Count the steps needed to count back from 20 to 0 in ones (20) and in twos (10)
Find the number just before 10, 20, 30, 40 (9, 19, 29, 39)
Numbers ending in 9 form a column pattern on the chart
Diagonal pattern on the chart increases by 11 (1, 12, 23 ... 100)
Describe a pattern seen in coloured numbers on the chart
On a 1-100 chart, the number above is 10 less and the number below is 10 more
The number to the right is 1 more and to the left is 1 less
Fill missing numbers in a window cut from the number chart
Observe how the number of blocks grows in each step of a pattern
Extend a growing block pattern and count blocks in the next shape
Square-shaped block patterns (1, 4, 9 blocks)
Shadows of people, trees and animals form when light is blocked
A shadow is seen when an object is in light and vanishes when there is no light
Shine a torch on objects and observe shadow shapes
Moving the torch changes the size of the shadow
Our shadow is longest in early morning/evening and shortest at noon

sections.name: 4.3 Let us Trace: shapes from outlines

concepts.text: Trace outlines of objects (eraser, leaf, matchbox, sharpener) to get flat shapes
A solid's face traced on paper gives a 2D shape (circle, rectangle, square, triangle)
Name objects that give the same trace as a bottle cap (circle) or an eraser (rectangle)

sections.name: 4.4 Hide and Seek: 2D shapes in objects

concepts.text: Find circles in objects (clock, ball, round light, plate)
Find rectangles in objects (shoe box, photo frame, door mat, TV)
Find triangles in objects (cap, wall hanging, slice)
Find squares in objects (dice face, square table top)

sections.name: 4.5 Colour the Carpet and Make Your Own Design

concepts.text: Identify triangles, circles, rectangles and squares in a pattern and colour by shape
Create a design using different 2D shapes
A corner is where two straight edges meet
A rectangle (table top) has 4 corners; children stand at corners or between them
A round object has no corners
Sort objects with straight edges and with curved edges
Objects with curved edges have 0 corners
Some objects have both straight and curved edges (gas cylinder, pipe)
Fold paper to make a square; a square has 4 corners and 4 edges
Fold a square along a diagonal to get a triangle with 3 corners and 3 edges
Fold and unfold to make more triangles and count corners
Make a paper dog face by folding a triangle

sections.name: 4.8 Patterns with shapes (stamping, hand and leaf prints)

concepts.text: Make patterns by stamping objects (bottle caps, erasers, pencils, corn)
Trace your hand to make a mehndi-style pattern
Make a leaf-print pattern by painting and pressing leaves
A pattern repeats shapes or colours in a fixed order

sections.name: 4.9 Extend the patterns (shape and number patterns)

concepts.text: Extend a repeating shape pattern
Number patterns from jumps on tiles (1, 4, 7, 10 ... adds 3; 1, 6, 11 ... adds 5)
Find the rule (how much is added each time) in a number pattern
Make a wall hanging from cut-outs of different 2D shapes

sections.name: 5.1 Let us Do: Lines in yoga asanas

concepts.text: Observe body positions in yoga asanas as lines
Standing (vertical) lines go straight up and down
Sleeping (horizontal) lines go side to side
Slanting lines are tilted, neither standing nor sleeping
Curved lines bend and are not straight
Sort asanas by the lines they show (vertical, slanting, curved, horizontal)
Try asanas and talk about the lines the body makes
A straight line does not bend; a curved line bends
Identify straight and curved lines in objects around us
Trace missing vertical, horizontal, slanting and curved lines in a picture
Join dots with straight lines to make new shapes (squares, rectangles, houses)
Use vertical, horizontal and slanting lines to draw figures on a dot grid
Draw figures using curved lines (clouds, rainbow)
Lines in letters and numbers (L, H, A, V, 7)

sections.name: 5.4 Let us Do: Designs with lines

concepts.text: Make a drawing using any two types of lines
Make a design using any three types of lines
Make a design using all types of lines
Zig-zag lines are made by joining slanting lines
Folding paper makes a crease that forms a straight line
More folds make more creases; trace straight lines red and slanting lines blue
Compete to make the most creases by folding
Try to make curved lines by folding paper
Each garland has 10 flowers; count flowers in tens
Complete a table of garlands and flowers from a picture
Find total flowers used by two children by adding

sections.name: 6.2 Let us do it on Ginladi! / Addition on the number line

concepts.text: Add by moving beads on a ginladi
Add on a number line by jumping forward (in tens and ones)
Read jumps on a number line and fill boxes to complete the addition

sections.name: 6.3 Playing with Blocks (addition with tens and ones)

concepts.text: Find the total number of blocks using tens rods and ones
Add 2-digit numbers by adding ones, then tens (without regrouping)
Add 2-digit numbers with regrouping: 10 ones make 1 ten (carry over)
Column addition of 2-digit numbers

sections.name: 6.4 Let us Do: Addition word problems

concepts.text: Word problems on finding a total (runs in two matches, 43 + 58)
Word problems on getting more (pencils, marbles, money spent, people on a bus)
Totals that go beyond 100 (e.g. 43 + 58 = 101)

sections.name: 6.5 Let us Count Diyas (subtraction with ginladi)

concepts.text: Take away diyas and find how many are left using a ginladi
Subtraction means taking away or finding what is left

sections.name: 6.6 Subtraction on the number line and with blocks

concepts.text: Subtract by jumping backward on a number line
Subtract 2-digit numbers using blocks (37 - 24) without regrouping
Subtract 2-digit numbers with regrouping: break 1 ten into 10 ones (borrow)
Column subtraction of 2-digit numbers

sections.name: 6.7 Let us Do / Decorating with Garlands (subtraction word problems)

concepts.text: Money left after buying something (82 - 22, 60 - 20)
Flowers left after giving some away (28 - 5, 73 - 47)
Things left after some are lost, sold or used (shells, passengers, balloons, bangles)
Find how many more are needed to reach a target (20 skips, did 14)
Missing addend problems: start + ? = total (56 birds + ? = 87)
Counting on to find a difference (18 taps to 35)
Addition and subtraction are related; one addition fact gives two subtraction facts
Complete a fact family by filling missing numbers
Changing the order of numbers in addition does not change the sum
Each block in a pyramid is the sum of the two blocks below it
Find missing numbers in a pyramid using addition or subtraction
Complete similar number diagrams

sections.name: 6.11 Hania and Mansi's Gift (two-step money problem)

concepts.text: Add two costs to find total money spent (24 + 37)
Subtract total spent from money in hand to find money left (78 - 61)
Check worked addition and subtraction sums and correct the wrong ones
Find common mistakes in carrying and borrowing

sections.name: 7.1 Let us Do: Measuring length with non-standard units

concepts.text: Measure the length of objects using a book or other non-standard units
Different units give different counts for the same length
Find the shortest route to reach school quickly
Choose the longest path between two points
Draw the shortest path between two points
Measure heights of animals in blocks (giraffe 9 blocks, camel 7, monkey 2)
Compare heights: taller, shorter, tallest, shortest
Trace your hand on squared paper and count lines to find its length
Body measures like hand span and steps can be used to measure
Compare weights of vegetables and fruits: heavier and lighter
Bigger size does not always mean heavier
Find the heaviest and lightest object in a group
Fill in blanks with heavier than / lighter than

sections.name: 7.6 Let us Do: Ordering by weight

concepts.text: Collect objects (paper, eraser, pencil box, bag) and find lightest and heaviest
Arrange objects in increasing order of weight
Estimate weight by lifting objects in hands
On a balance, the heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up
Mark objects as light (L) or heavy (H) using a balance picture
Same-size bags of sand and dry leaves have different weights (sand is heavier)
Types of weighing balances used by people (shop balance, weighing machine)

sections.name: 7.8 Fruits in the Park: Balancing with units

concepts.text: Find how many smaller fruits balance a bigger one (6 mangoes balance a watermelon)
Use balancing to compare weights through a common unit
Measure ingredients by spoons and glasses to make lemonade
Scale the quantity of ingredients for more glasses
Find how many glasses of water fill a bottle
Compare capacity: holds more, less or equal water
Name friends whose bottles hold equal, less or more water
Measure a wall, bed and door with a chosen unit (eraser, blocks, pencil) and record
Compare your weight with family and friends; find places to check weight

sections.name: 8.1 Let us Do: Counting equal groups

concepts.text: Count total wheels on cars (7 cars, 4 wheels each = 28)
Count wings of butterflies, legs of octopuses, soldiers in rows
Equal groups can be counted by repeated addition
Multiplication is a short way to add equal groups (7 x 4 = 28)
Read 'groups of' as times (4 groups of 10 = 4 x 10)

sections.name: 8.2 Complete the Table and Match the Following

concepts.text: Write number of groups, number in each group and total in a table
Match repeated addition with multiplication statements and pictures
Build the table of 2 by skip counting in 2s
Build the table of 3
Build the table of 5
Build the table of 10
4 groups of 3 and 3 groups of 4 both give 12
Changing the order of numbers in multiplication does not change the product
Write multiplication sentences from pictures of groups (4 x 5, 5 x 4, 6 x 4, 4 x 6)
Find the total in packets with equal items (8 packets of 5 bindis)
Buttons on shirts, people in cars
Cost of several items at the same price (6 pencils at Rs 4 each)
Make the table of 4 by doubling the table of 2
Make the table of 8 by adding tables of 2 and 6
Arrange objects in rows and columns (arrays) to write multiplication facts
Share things equally so everyone gets the same number
Check whether a sharing is equal or not
Find how many each person gets in equal sharing

sections.name: 8.8 Let us Do: Sharing by drawing

concepts.text: Draw 12 bindis equally on 2 ice-cream cones
Redistribute laddoos from 2 plates equally onto 3 plates

sections.name: 8.9 Let us Make: Grouping and sharing word problems

concepts.text: Find how many groups can be made (21 beads, 7 per string = 3 strings)
Find number of bracelets, vases or shirts from a total and group size
Find how many in each group when shared equally (27 candles in 3 boxes)
Division as repeated subtraction or making equal groups
Sharing and grouping are linked to multiplication facts
Seasons in India: summer, rainy (monsoon), autumn, winter, spring
Relate vacations, birthdays and favourite activities to seasons
Describe what is special about each season
Match seasons with their names and festivals celebrated in them
A year has 12 months in a fixed order (January to December)
Read a calendar and fill a table of months and their number of days
Months have 30 or 31 days; February has 28 days (29 in a leap year)
A leap year comes once in four years
A week has 7 days; names and order of days

sections.name: 9.4 Let us Talk: Using a calendar

concepts.text: We use a calendar to know dates and days
Count how many Sundays are in a month
Find months with 5 Sundays in a calendar
Name months of summer and winter vacations
Add days of two months to find the total (30 + 31 = 61)
Match activities with the time they take (seconds, minutes, hours, days)
Compare which activity takes more or less time

sections.name: 9.6 Let us Talk: Family Trip (dates and duration)

concepts.text: Find the length of a trip from start and return dates (24 to 28 November = 5 days)
Find duration in hours of day trips and the return time
Compare durations of train journeys to find which took longer
A clock has an hour hand (short) and a minute hand (long)
Read time to the hour (o'clock) on a clock face
Relate daily activities to times (wake up, school, lunch)

sections.name: 9.8 Let us Do: Reading and drawing clock times

concepts.text: Read the time shown on clocks
Draw hour and minute hands to show a given time
Show times of your own daily activities on a clock
Four main directions: north, south, east, west
Use a compass/direction marker on a classroom map
Tell position of one object relative to another using directions
Describe a route as moving in one direction then another

sections.name: 10.1 How Much I Spent? (money at the fair)

concepts.text: Add prices of rides to find total money spent
Find money spent from money given and money left (40 - 3 = 37)

sections.name: 10.2 Let us Do: Indian coins and notes

concepts.text: Recognise Indian coins (Rs 1, 2, 5, 10, 20) and notes (Rs 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500)
Find money needed to buy items shown in pictures
Observe a Rs 500 note: amount written in words and in numerals
Pictures on notes show monuments (Red Fort on Rs 500)
1 rupee = 100 paise
Four 25-paise coins make 1 rupee
Five 20-paise coins make 1 rupee
Add the money won from popped balloons of different values
Choose balloons to make a given amount
Choose balloons to win the largest possible amount with 3 or 4 chances

sections.name: 10.5 Let us Do: Different ways to pay an amount

concepts.text: Make an amount (e.g. Rs 66) using different combinations of notes and coins
Use fewest notes and coins to pay an amount
Find total cost of items bought
Find money left after buying
Decide what can be bought with the money in hand

sections.name: 10.7 Let us Do: Money word problems

concepts.text: Addition of money (Rs 25 pens + Rs 40 notebooks)
Find an amount that is more than another (Rs 43 and Rs 14 more)
Subtraction of money to find what is left (Rs 58 - Rs 48)

sections.name: 11.1 Favourite Colours (reading data from a picture)

concepts.text: Count children by dress colour and complete a table
Find the most liked and least liked colour
Compare two categories using 'more than' and 'less than'
Record favourite fruits in a table from a picture
Find total from a table and the count for one category
Find most and least liked fruit
Compare two categories: more than, less than or equal to
Discuss a picture and fill a table of modes of travel to school
Draw a pictograph using one face for one student
Read a pictograph to find most and least used mode
Compare two modes using the pictograph

sections.name: 11.4 Let us Do: Games we play

concepts.text: Count students by favourite game and complete a table
Show the data as a face chart (pictograph)
Find most and least liked game and compare games

sections.name: 11.5 Let us Do: Surveys (vegetables, family size)

concepts.text: Collect data by asking classmates about favourite vegetables
Organise survey data in a table and answer questions
Survey friends about the number of family members
Find the most common family size and the smallest family
Count families with more than a given number of members
Plan questions before a survey
Visit families and record data in a table
Count families with both, one or no grandparents
Connect matching shapes with non-crossing lines
Complete shape and number patterns
Number trick: think of a number, double, add, halve, subtract (always 4)
Count different routes or ways to reach a place
Write number names from 11 to 20
Match an object with its shadow
Matchstick puzzle: remove sticks to leave squares
'Who am I?' riddles about shapes and objects
Choose numbers that add up to a given total (30)
Make 2-digit numbers using one digit
Trace a path in a maze and answer questions about it
Count rectangles (including squares) formed by joining dots
Complete number sentences with + or -
Divide a region into equal parts with given objects in each
Arrange 1 to 7 so each arm of a figure has equal sum
Number of cuts to cut a 6 m cloth into 1 m pieces (5)
Find a number whose double is 18 (half of 18)
Make a target number by pressing calculator keys
